messages:
maria: Heads-up — we're seeing a repeat of slot pressure in eu-west dedicated pool starting ~08:45 UTC. Latency P99 for text-generation routes jumped from 180ms -> 1.8s and throughput dipped ~30%. Notified oncall.
jon: thanks — any obvious error rates or evictions?
maria: error rates flat, but node-level logs show a bunch of tenant KV cache evictions and kernel fallback events. snippet: `kernel_selector: chose cpu_fallback for model-abc seq_len=2048` repeated across hosts.
lee: that fallback looks suspicious. cpu_fallback should only happen for oom or unsupported kernels. Can you paste profiling output from 08:44-08:46?
maria: pasting small segment: ```
[08:45:02] profile: model-abc batch_size=1 seq=2048 hw=V100 kernel=quant_gemm latency=170ms
[08:45:03] selector: estimated throughput mismatch -> chosen=cpu_fallback (est_latency=900ms)
[08:45:03] kvcache: evict tenant=tenA pages=12 reason=hot_eviction
[08:45:04] scheduler: packer merged small reqs -> large packet size=4096 tokens
```
ashley: noticed an autoscaler config change yesterday for eu-west dedicated quota pools — some tenants got a new min_slots=2 override. Could be bin-packing causing noisy neighbor effects.
jon: interesting — so two possible contributors: kernel selection heuristics misestimating latency for long sequences, and packing/batching merging cold and hot requests, causing KV churn.
lee: agree. Also saw a regression in the kernel latency model deployed in last release (runtimes/service: v2.14.0). The model predicts kernel latency from sequence length distribution; looks like the training set didn't include many long seqs.
maria: repro steps from a dev host: 
1) send concurrent mix: 200x seq=32 short + 40x seq=2048 long
2) observe packer grouping and kernel selector switching to cpu_fallback

Observed: P99 spike, KV cache evictions on tenants processing long seqs, eviction cascades to unrelated tenants (noisy neighbor).
jon: can we confirm node-level GPU memory pressure? or is it purely selector decision?
maria: GPUs report available memory ~5% but not full. No OOM logs. Selector logs show `fallback_reason=latency_model_mismatch`.
lee: so the selector predicted GPU kernel would be slower than cpu_fallback for those batches — that means the latency estimator is inverted for long sequences after the new heuristics.
ashley: quick mitigation: revert the latency estimator model to v2.13.2 in eu-west routing via rollout config? We can also pin heavy tenants to dedicated pools temporarily.
jon: SLO action plan: 1) immediate rollback of selector model in eu-west 2) add a temporary cap on packer merging (max_packet_tokens=2048) 3) increase KV cache quota for affected tenants to avoid hot_eviction cascades 4) follow-up perf regression postmortem.
lee: I'm on rollback. Starting canary to 10% then 100% if green.
ashley: I'll add a routing rule to pin top-5 heavy seq tenants to separate pools and raise their kv cache limit by +30%.
infra-bot: deployment v2.13.2-latency-estimator rollback started by lee at 08:52 UTC — canary 10% -> monitoring.
sre-oncall: alerting: p99 latency back to ~220ms in canary subset. Rolling to 100% if stable for 5m.
maria: monitoring shows p99 trending down in 10% nodes, but a few hosts still show eviction bursts — those hosts had older kernel binaries (some mismatch in compile flags).
lee: noted — taking those hosts out of rotation and redeploying consistent kernels. Also will add a quick check in the selector: if gpu_mem_available < 15% then prefer GPU kernels even if estimator predicts otherwise (to avoid unnecessary cpu fallback when memory fine).
jon: pls capture perf counters for one affected host: `nvidia-smi dmon` and `perf stat -e cycles,instructions` during a repro run. We need numbers for postmortem.
maria: captured and uploaded logs to /mnt/logs/incident-2155127777/ — key findings: GPU compute utilization stayed ~65%, kernel exec time for quant_gemm on long seqs actually 120-150ms not 900ms as estimator predicted. Estimator bug confirmed.
ashley: suggest we add long-seq synthetic workloads to estimator retraining set and add a unit test in CI to avoid regression.
lee: agree. Also adjusting packer heuristics: don't merge short latency-sensitive reqs with long-seq ones; add route-level hints to prefer isolated batches for `chat-stream` customers.
jon: owning the postmortem. Draft timeline: detection 08:45, rollback start 08:52, p99 partially recovered 08:56 (canary), full recovery 09:02 after kernel redeploy. Root cause: latency estimator regression + packer merging + quota/pinning config that amplified noisy neighbor eviction cascades.
maria: will open infra tickets: 1) KV quota audit for eu-west pools 2) packer config safe defaults 3) latency-estimator retrain + CI checks.
ashley: I'll communicate to affected account managers that we mitigated and are adding protections; SRE to confirm no SLA breach callbacks.
lee: follow-ups: add a fast-path in selector to consult recent empirical kernel timing (last 5 minutes) to avoid stale estimator decisions.
jon: thanks team. adding severity=high-2 to this incident and scheduling a 1h postmortem tomorrow.
infra-bot: incident-2155127777 status: mitigated -> monitor.
